entities.summary: Acharya Pingala was an ancient Indian poet and mathematician who authored the Chanda\u00b3stra, a foundational treatise on Sanskrit prosody. Born in the 2nd century BCE, Pingala was a key figure in the development of Sanskrit grammar and poetry. His work, the Pingala Sutras, was composed around 100 CE and remains a significant contribution to the field of Sanskrit prosody. Pingala's influence extended beyond the realm of Sanskrit to the development of Indian mathematics and astronomy. His most notable work, the Chanda\u00b3stra, is a comprehensive guide to Sanskrit prosody, covering topics such as meter, rhythm, and phonetics. Pingala's legacy can be seen in the works of later Sanskrit scholars, who built upon his discoveries to further refine the study of Sanskrit prosody. The Chanda\u00b3stra has been preserved and transmitted through the centuries, remaining an essential resource for scholars of Sanskrit language and literature. Pingala's work has also had a lasting impact on the development of Indian mathematics, particularly in the field of number theory. His contributions to the field of Sanskrit prosody have had a lasting impact on the study of Sanskrit language and literature, and his work continues to be studied and respected by scholars today.
